newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Czechs agree on farm cooperation in EU bid.
newsitem.headline: Poland, Czechs agree on farm cooperation in EU bid.

text.p: The Polish and Czech agriculture ministers agreed on Monday to coordinate farming policies in their efforts to win membership of the European Union.

"There can be no question of competing in these efforts. We will cooperate, coordinate our actions and present common standpoints to Brussels," Poland's Jaroslaw Kalinowski said after meeting his Czech counterpart Josef Lux.
"We should focus our attention on preparations for EU membership negotiations and we should not do it separately," Lux added.
The ministers signed two agreements on mutual recognition of agriculture products' quality certificates, removing a major obstacle in bilateral farm trade.

But there was no sign of agreement on a timetable for scrapping customs duties for agricultural goods among members of the Central European Free Trade Agreement, whose other members are Hungary, Slovakia and Slovenia.
Lux also said Prague favoured scrapping all farm duties as of January 1 next year but Kalinowski made clear he preferred a later date.
"We should not move blindly to liberalisation," Kalinowski said.

Analysts say Czech agriculture, which employs less than 10 percent of the workforce and where the average farm has 140 hectares, is better prepared for EU accession than that of Poland, which employs 28 percent of the workforce and where farms are very small.
